paragraphs: Shimon bar Chiya. Hyman describes him as a student of Rav, as in Eruvin ch. 5 halakha 5: "R' Ba bar Mamal, Shimon bar Chiya in the name of Rav"; and in Avodah Zarah ch. 4 halakha 8: "Shimon bar Chiya was teaching Chiya bar Rav: From when does a gentile make wine prohibited as libation wine? From when he understands idolatry. Rav Yoshiyah brought out a tractate [מכלתא] and said to him: This that you say, etc." And the Penei Moshe explained that R' Yoshiyah brought out from the מסב׳ [abbreviation left unresolved]

which he teaches, etc. And Hyman says, with all due respect to his honor, that he did not examine carefully: a small error fell into the Yerushalmi, and Hyman says one must read: "Rav put his head out of the window" [אפיק רב ראשיה מכוותא]. And Hyman explains that Shimon b. Ch[iya] was studying with Chiya bar Rav outside the study hall, and Rav, who sat inside and heard how they were studying, put his head out of the window and set them right on the truth. And likewise in Eruvin ch. 1 halakha 1: "Chananiah bar

Shelamia was sitting teaching Chiya bar Rav; Rav put his head out of the window." And likewise Beitzah ch. 5 halakha 1: "Rabbi looked out of the window." Hyman further says that a scribal error fell there, and one must read: "This that you say — regarding one who buys 'slaves' from a gentile," and not "grapes" (as my friend the great rabbi, author of Mishpachot Soferim, p. 31, note 116), and this is true. Those who say [teachings] in his name: we find Rav Yehuda in Shabbat, end of ch. 5,
and R' Layya (Ilai) in Shabbat ch. 7, end of halakha 1.

notes.text: The named Guggenheimer Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah4:8 gives the intelligible wine/idolatry question and retains the Yoshiyah/mikhilta wording. Hyman instead proposes that Rav put his head out of the window. The precise compressed Penei Moshe explanation still requires its actual commentary text.
The same named Yerushalmi text reads grapes. Hyman, citing Mishpachot Soferim p.31 note116, argues for slaves. The attested reading and his proposed correction remain distinct.
The supplied Layya (Ilai) name variant is retained.

The whole printed notice is in volume III, p. 1174. The consulted whole Guggenheimer Avodah Zarah 4:8 paragraph retains Rav Yoshiyah, mikhilta and grapes. The corresponding whole Penei Moshe comments, in the Piotrków 1898–1900 digital edition, explicitly say that Chiyya asked Shimon the question, and explain Yoshiyah as bringing out of the tractate he teaches in Avodah Zarah: הוציא ממסכת דתני הוא בע״ז. The English therefore renders מכלתא as a tractate rather than the inherited baraita. Hyman’s supplied מסב׳ remains visible and unchanged; this actual commentary comparison supplements the older notes that said the commentary had not been inspected. Hyman’s criticism of Penei Moshe, his definite proposed Rav-head-out-of-window reading, his outside/inside study-hall reconstruction, and his emphatic slaves-NOT-grapes correction remain his arguments. The whole Eruvin 1:1 comparison directly has Chananiah bar Shelemya teaching Chiyya son of Rav and Rav putting his head out of the window; it supports that comparison without proving the proposed replacement of Yoshiyah in Avodah Zarah. The whole Eruvin 5:5 paragraph directly has Ba bar Mamal and Shimon bar Chiyya in the name of Rav; it does not independently establish all of Hyman’s teacher chronology. The exact Mishpachot Soferim p. 31 note 116 and the other supplied Shabbat and Beitzah locators have not been newly collated. No title is transferred between abbreviated occurrences and no namesakes are merged. All current notes remain verbatim.
